newsitem.title: USA: National Computer buys McGraw-Hill units.
newsitem.headline: National Computer buys McGraw-Hill units.

text.p: National Computer Systems Inc, an educational computer services company, said Tuesday it is acquiring McGraw-Hill School Systems and McGraw-Hill/London House, divisions of The McGraw-Hill Cos for about $29 million.
The move is part of the company's strategy to build its presence in education and the rapidly evolving professional assessment and employee testing market, National Computer said.

McGraw-Hill School Systems is a supplier of student information management software and McGraw-Hill/London House is a supplier of pre-employment and employee assessment systems to business, industry and government. Fiscal 1996 revenues of these two businesses were about $25 million, National Computer said.
New York-based McGraw-Hill said the sale was part of its strategy to focus expansion on its curriculum and professional development products.
McGraw-Hill shares were up 9/16 at 59-3/8 Tuesday and National Computer shares were up 1/8 at 26-3/4.
